characters.name: Rail Steward Essi
characters.role: Keeper of the bell rail and repair docket

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: Hale has put his lunch tin in the loading shutter. It snaps shut hard enough to dent the lid. “Yesterday that was somebody’s handcart. My watch agreed with the rail when I looked. I signed it through.” He passes you the repair seal. “The Letter Gallery holds the rail record. Try them both against the watch before I sign anything else.”

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: The clock starts at twelve in each practice case. Compare its first reading to the separate drum. Then advance the trial one minute. See what can happen in a case that agrees at the start.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: In two cases the first readings agreed. Only one watch moved on the next minute. The third watch showed twelve against an eleven reading and stayed there. Someone could agree about the time at that first glance and still have a watch that cannot carry them through the shift.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: I can sign a record of a test I made. The stamp has that test’s date. The shift crew keeps a way to compare the watch again when the record grows old.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Look for a source that tells you how someone checked a claim. The old optics note records a way of testing. The Mill note asks what happens when nobody challenges an accepted belief. Neither writer signed our watch slip.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The rail crew has a separate drum and can check the watch through two marks. That asks someone to be there before loading. A dated seal can let one crew use a test already carried out, as long as they know when it expires. Which direction shall we put on the first docket?

options.text: Start each shift with a rail comparison.
Use the dated repair record and its fallback.
Leave the docket open for now.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi sends a checker to the independent drum. The opening docket now asks for the first time and the next advancing minute. A match at one mark stays on the slip until the second mark completes the check.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi clips the seal and test date to the docket. A crew can use that shift’s signed result. If the seal breaks or the date is missing or old, the fallback sends someone to the independent rail for both marks.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A courier came just as the shutter started to fall. There is a reply by the stair rail. Check what the courier can see and hear by the shutter.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The two crews are together for just a short part of the shift. Someone behind the shutter can miss one mark even when the check happens. Give that person a way to see or hear both readings before their hands fill with crates.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.
I kept both landing sheets on the island.
I checked what someone could see from the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: You kept the original result when a loading condition changed. Our first check stays on its own docket too. The shutter changes how long people can share that check. Give the shorter overlap its own line.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The lamps were clear from one approach and gone from another. Here the first call is clear at the rail and muffled beside the shutter. Give the person who starts there their own way to follow the two marks.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi moves a second checker to the shutter before it falls. The rail checker calls both readings separately. The checker at the shutter repeats each one back for the waiting courier. The first docket stays signed.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi pins separate opening and next-minute marks where the courier can see them before lifting a crate. The first docket stays signed. Both marks point back to the independent drum.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A new checker can use the marks and the dated docket. They have asked where the test came from if they need to check again after a long repair.

options.text: Leave a wide copy of the check instructions.
Keep the docket at the rail.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi hangs the wider copy near the entrance. It leaves lines for who checked, which drum they used, and when. The dated first docket and its fallback stay with the repair slip.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The entrance copy tells a new checker where the original date and comparison belong. There is space for the next dated check beside it.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: One spare dial can go out before the shift starts. At the rail, an apprentice can stand with the crew and ask about the marks. Some people leave before handover. At the low slot, a person can stop with a cart and check with the keeper when they arrive.

options.text: Set the practice dial at the shared rail.
Set the practice dial in the low slot.
Leave the spare dial inside for now.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The people at handover pass the dial along. An apprentice asks which reading came from the reference. The crew lead takes them back through the two marks before they go.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A helper parks their cart beside the spare dial and turns it through the two marks. They missed handover, so the keeper shows them which mark to compare with the rail record.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: We need a handover before the next open hearing. The runner can point people to the place. They also need to know when to come. Will you try a practice run with us? Hesper has the blank clips. Sefa says the rail can hear her from anywhere. Kip says we should stand somewhere and find out.

options.text: Bring Lark’s full order to Hesper’s bench.
Bring Lark’s clipped strips to Hesper’s bench.
Bring Lark’s caller sheet to Hesper’s bench.
Bring Emberford’s paired stubs to Hesper’s bench.
Bring Hana’s relay ticket to Hesper’s bench.
Bring Emberford’s appointment rota to Hesper’s bench.
Start a new packet with the blank slips.
Leave the bench ready for later.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: You sent the full sheet. The landing queue could see the order. The outside stalls waited for it. Keep the time and place together this time, even when Sefa only has one breath.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: You sent the linked strips out to the stalls. One clip came loose. Hesper, can you put the bell beside the place on the same strip this time?

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: You gave us time to check the sheets. The landing crew had to take a hand off the hoist to call the turns. Write the whole call down so the next reader can carry it without another trip.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: You left the matched pickup stubs on my counter. The tick let us join the kettle to its owner and keep the fee slate inside. Use the matching mark for Hale’s docket.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: You sent our tray through Hana’s stall. She could check that it was ours without opening the fee slip. Here, keep a return edge so Kip can carry a change back to us.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: You left us our private appointments. The board told people when to return. Give Hale a mark for the bell and the place where someone can check it.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: These slips belong to this practice run. I signed a separate timing docket before Sefa tried the call. Hesper can make us a packet. Leave my original in its clip for a second check.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: One piece of paper ought to reach the far end with its time still attached. Seat the clip on the short end and leave a corner for the checker.

options.text: Fold the bell line beside the place on one strip.
Match the two notches, then turn the flap over.
Clip a new strip across the two printed lines.
Set the clip down.

dialogue.speaker: smith-hesper
dialogue.text: There. You can lift the packet by the corner. The time, place and small reference mark all stay on the paper.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: At our ferry, older hands teach the call in pairs. One says the place and time. The other says both back before anyone moves. I’ll take the rail and Kip will wait with the packet. Take the passage to hear what gets through this time.

options.text: Keep the quick doorway call that you and Vesper tried.
Give Sefa the opening call.
Let Sefa rest her voice.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: You gave an usher a line that helped someone find the stage. This time we need the runner to keep a time as well as a place. Keep the paper with Kip while I speak.

options.text: Go back to the practice line.

dialogue.speaker: scholar-sefa
dialogue.text: “At the next bell, bring the signed practice copy to the low bench.” Sefa folds her arms and waits to hear it back.

dialogue.speaker: kip-arden
dialogue.text: I heard “low bench” and thought they meant now. The passage swallowed the time. Here, lift the clip. The slip has the words I missed. Shall I carry the whole line back? I can finish one sentence before I ask my next question.

options.text: Have Kip echo the whole line and carry the slip back.
Let Kip keep the packet for a moment.

dialogue.speaker: kip-arden
dialogue.text: “At the next bell, bring the signed practice copy to the low bench.” Same place. Now I can tell when to set out too. Rook wants the slip and Hale’s own docket at the rail.

dialogue.speaker: rook-tamsin
dialogue.text: Kip first heard the bench and took it to mean come now. A runner has scribbled NOW on the shorthand draft. Kip read the rest from the packet. Those two agree because Kip read it. Lay Hale’s signed docket over the draft to check the time against another record.

options.text: Recall what Rook checked for the family at the well.
Slide Hale’s signed docket beside the packet.
Go get the original docket and runner’s reply.

dialogue.speaker: rook-tamsin
dialogue.text: You asked me to show the family when I made the check. Spring answers for spring. This docket gives the time for one practice run. Read the little line above my thumb.

options.text: Return to the docket comparison.

dialogue.speaker: rook-tamsin
dialogue.text: Hale’s own line gives the next bell. Turn the NOW strip under it. The bench stays the same. The instruction tells us when to bring this packet. The next hearing needs its own signed time.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The call told Kip where to go. The copy carried the time through the passage. We can leave both lines on a low board. Or we can keep the ferry’s call and answer here, with two people free to say back what reached them.

options.text: Set the checked pair on the low board.
Give the runner a checked slip and post a relay shift.
Leave the checked pair on the worktable.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A visitor rests a bundle under the low board and reads the place and bell in order. Someone who needs to hear them still waits until a keeper is free to read them aloud.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Hesper fits another clip. Sefa takes the rail, Kip takes the bench and Rook leaves the signed time beside both. A runner will wait while someone reads the line back. That takes a hand away from the next copy.

cards.title: John Stuart Mill on challenge (1859)
cards.text: In chapter 2 of On Liberty, Mill argues that an accepted view can be true and still need a serious challenge. Encountering reasons and objections can help people understand the view they hold.
cards.limits: Mill’s argument concerns how people hold and discuss beliefs. It is separate from the Council’s fictional watch trial.

missions.title: When the Hand Moves
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What else needs to hold after a watch gives the right time once?
missions.stake: If the hall sets its time by a watch that only agrees with itself, nobody can say when the repair really happened.

objectives.title: Find Hale at the Council’s workshop watch.
Read the two source notes, the independent rail record and the repair seal.
Advance all three cases at the watch and compare the changes.

kq.action: compare a true reading with evidence that the watch advances

objectives.title: Give the loading crew a check they can use.
Read the courier’s reply and check the view by the shutter.
Keep the first docket and give both crews the next time check.

kq.action: make the same check available to people on both sides of the shutter

missions.title: A New Checker
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can someone find the basis of a test carried out by another crew?

objectives.title: Put a wide copy of the check near the entrance.

missions.title: A Dial for Handover
missions.knowledgeQuestion: Who gets a chance to see or question how a timing mark was made?

objectives.title: Check the crew’s handover and the low practice slot.
Place the spare dial and see who can use it.

missions.title: The Handover Before the Bell
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What lets a team check that a message and its limits reached the next person?

objectives.title: Make a packet, carry the call and compare the reply with the signed docket.
Choose a place for the checked pair and see who uses it.

journal.text: A stopped watch shared the drum’s first reading. Its next mark showed the limit of the match. Both loading crews now have a way to follow the check.

journal.title: The handover before the bell
journal.text: Hesper put the two lines together. Sefa made the call, and Kip found the time the call lost. Rook kept Hale’s own docket beside the reply. We left a way for the next reader to check both.

moments.did: You compared cases that agreed on the first mark and checked the next one.
moments.prompt: What does a second look show that the first match leaves open?

moments.did: You helped a courier on the other side of the shutter take part in the check.
moments.prompt: Where would you stand for both readings to be clear?

chronicle.title: The signed clock docket
chronicle.text: The loading crew has a way to check the watch. The docket names the separate drum or the dated repair test.

chronicle.title: Two marks at the shutter
chronicle.text: A courier needed both readings. The revised instruction gives the short overlap its own check while keeping the original docket.
